firmware.title: Build and install screen firmware
firmware.intro: The built-in ESPHome CLI uses your own profile (YAML with keys) and secrets. Choose the screen's profile, then a USB port (screen connected to the Home Assistant machine), {ota} with the hostname, or {download} to put the firmware on the screen from your own computer. {check} only validates, {build} compiles, {install} puts the firmware on the screen. Your tiles stay as they are in ESP Screens. The first build takes a few minutes.

alerts.title: A full-screen notification, from an automation.
alerts.intro: Every screen has the {action} action. It places a card over everything, wakes the screen, and keeps the backlight at normal brightness until someone taps the button or the timeout runs out. Home Assistant itself shows no explanation or dropdowns for ESPHome actions; everything you can fill in is listed here.
alerts.loading: The cheatsheet is still loading; one moment.

try.title: Title
try.subtitle: Subtitle
try.flash_hint: Four times when the alert arrives.

howto.add: {add} and search for {esphome}. Choose your screen's action: Home Assistant calls it "Performs the action show_alert of the node {device}".
howto.fields: {bold} Home Assistant asks for all seven; leave what you don't use empty ({empty}, {zero}, off).
howto.yaml: Prefer YAML? Choose {edit} on the action and paste the example below.

all.title: All screens at once
all.text: Fire the event {show} with the same fields, and ESP Screens passes the alert on to every screen that is online, including screens you add later. {dismiss} clears it everywhere. In an automation, add the {event} action or paste the example under {edit}. Leave out the fields you don't use. ESP Screens has to be running for this.

fields.text: Text is free-form; the limit is in bytes, and an accented letter counts as two. What doesn't fit gets an ellipsis (title) or is dropped (subtitle).

icons.text: Fill in the name in {field}, for example {example}. {mdi} and the hex codepoint ({hex}) also work. Only these icons are included in the firmware; any other name shows the warning triangle. Tap an icon to copy its name.
icons.extra: Also available: control and weather icons
icons.none: No icon for "{query}". Unknown names show the warning triangle ({fallback}).

colors.text: Fill in the name in {field}. These are the pastel shades of the tiles, with dark text. Empty or unknown gives the white card. Tap to copy.

behaviour.wakes: {bold} An alert immediately wakes a dimmed or dark screen and appears above every page, every open light card, and the standby layer.
behaviour.on: {bold} As long as the card is showing, the backlight stays at normal brightness. Standby and night hours wait. After the button, the regular standby time starts again.
behaviour.timeout: {bold} {zero} waits for the button, however long that takes. With {minute} the card disappears after a minute, but the button closes it sooner.
behaviour.blinking: {bold} {flash} blinks the backlight four times when the alert arrives (about a second) and leaves the screen on afterward.
behaviour.replacing: {bold} A new alert replaces the current one; there's no stack. The replaced alert reports itself as {replaced}.
behaviour.closing: {bold} {dismiss} clears the card, for example if the door is already open. Without an alert, that action does nothing.
behaviour.beside: {bold} does nothing; only the button closes it. That way a wake-up tap never accidentally dismisses the alert.

events.text: Every end fires the event {event} with {action}, {title}, {screen} (the device name) and the {device_id} that Home Assistant adds. Visible under Settings → Tools → Events.
events.wait: Waiting until someone presses the button

tips.color: Use a {bold}: orange for the door, red for smoke or water, green for "done". The text always stays dark and readable.
tips.short: Keep the title {bold}; a screen shows about twenty characters on one line and ends a longer title with an ellipsis. Put details in the subtitle.
tips.button: A {bold} turns the notification into a question: "Coming", "Seen", "Turn off". The event then tells you who responded.
tips.resolve: For an alert that resolves itself (the door opens, the laundry gets taken out) close it in the same automation with {dismiss}.
tips.every: Every screen? Fire {event} once (see All screens at once). The screens still work independently and each reports with its own {screen}.
tips.claude: Rather {bold} for the automation? Install the ESP Screens skill under Settings → Claude.
